topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: Why Colliding Blocks Compute Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students or curious science enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: The Impossible Puzzle (1 minute)
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
A small mass hits a massive block.
The big block then hits a wall.
How many collisions happen in total?
The count surprisingly reveals Pi digits.
animations: Create a central object labeled 'Puzzle' in #FFFFFF.
Fade in label 'Physics' #FF5733 below 'Puzzle'.
Show 'Geometry' #33FF57 beside 'Puzzle' as a cloud.
Animate 'Puzzle' vibrating slowly to imply difficulty.
Flash 'Conclusion' #3357FF once to signify the goal.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws (1 minute)
lecture_lines: Conservation of momentum must hold true.
Kinetic energy remains constant throughout collisions.
These rules dictate block velocity changes.
animations: Display 'Momentum' #FFD700 formula p=mv in center.
Animate vector arrow pointing right with label 'v'.
Show another object colliding, color changed to #FF4500.

sections.title: Mapping Collisions to Geometry (1.5 minutes)
lecture_lines: We map velocities to a 2D plane.
Each collision is a reflection in space.
The point traces an arc of a circle.
Energy conservation keeps the path fixed.
Collisions hit the circle's boundaries perfectly.
animations: Draw a billiard ball path as a line.
Transition path into a geometric arc in #00FFFF.
Highlight intersection point with color #FFFF00.
Animate path tracing along the arc slowly.
Fade out arc leaving point visible in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Arc and the Angle (1 minute)
lecture_lines: The circle radius represents total energy.
Arc segments measure the circle's circumference.
Angle segments correspond to Pi divisions.
Mass ratios determine the arc lengths.
The physics problem becomes pure geometry.
animations: Show a circular arc with center labeled 'C' #FFFFFF.
Display angle theta changing as arc extends.
Flash the intersection point with #FF4500.
Move indicator along the arc showing theta growth.
Label the total angle value as Pi #FFFF00.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Abstraction (0.5 minutes)
lecture_lines: Bouncing blocks solve a trigonometric puzzle.
Hidden symmetry reveals universal constant Pi.
Simple mechanics yield profound mathematical truth.
animations: Draw a circle representing 'Abstract World' #FFFFFF.
Fade in all previous geometric concepts inside the circle.
Show final text 'Q.E.D.' in #00FFFF.
